section: Environmental legislation in India - Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Environment (Protection) Act 1986
subsections: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order of their enactment:
A. Forest (Conservation) Act
B. Environment (Protection) Act
C. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
D. National Green Tribunal Act
accepted.x: The Water Act was enacted in 1974, the Forest (Conservation) Act in 1980, the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 and the National Green Tribunal Act in 2010.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last items as anchors, then place the middle enactments by year.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first pollution-control law among the enactments listed below?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
accepted.x: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, is described as India’s first pollution law and also created the pollution-control Boards.
accepted.tq: Identify the earliest specialised pollution statute rather than the later umbrella law.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 came into force on:
accepted.x: The Water Act came into force on 23 March 1974.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commencement date from the year of enactment.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act:
1. It was enacted on 29 March 1981.
2. It came into force on 16 May 1981.
3. It followed the framework of the Water Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Air Act was enacted on 29 March 1981, commenced on 16 May 1981 and adopted the institutional framework of the Water Act.
accepted.tq: Check each date and the institutional relationship before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to amendments is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Water Act was amended in 1988, while the Air Act was amended in 1987 and again in 1988.
accepted.tq: Pair each statute with its specific amendment years and reject shifted dates.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 primarily imposed a cess on water consumed by:
o: Agricultural farms and forest departments בלבד
accepted.x: The Water Cess Act imposed a cess on water consumed by industries and local bodies. The associated Cess Rules were made in 1978.
accepted.tq: Focus on the specified liable users instead of the broader group of water consumers.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal significance of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980?
o: It required Central approval for diversion of forest land.
It transferred all forests to local bodies.
It established the National Green Tribunal.
accepted.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 made Central approval necessary for diversion of forest land.
accepted.tq: Match the statute with its distinctive regulatory function rather than its subject in general terms.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

accepted.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is popularly known as an umbrella legislation because it:
o: creates only judicial authorities for environmental disputes
coordinates the Central and State authorities created under the Water and Air Acts
accepted.x: The Act provides an umbrella framework to coordinate the Central and State authorities established under the Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional meaning of a familiar descriptive term.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the primary purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: To regulate only the use of forest land
To protect and improve the environment and control pollution
To levy a cess on municipal water consumption
To establish a specialised environmental tribunal
accepted.x: The Act provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling pollution.
accepted.tq: Match the umbrella statute with its broad statutory purpose, not with a related specialised law.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the primary authority responsible for environmental protection is the:
accepted.x: The Central Government is the primary authority under the Environment (Protection) Act.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the statutory authority.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s:
Which of the following powers may be exercised by the Central Government under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Laying down emission and discharge standards
2. Regulating the location of industries
3. Managing hazardous wastes
4. Protecting public health
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Central Government’s powers include prescribing emission and discharge standards, regulating industrial locations, managing hazardous wastes and protecting public health.
accepted.tq: Treat a comprehensive list of statutory powers as correct only after checking every item.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Directions issued by the Central Government under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 may include:
o: appointment of judges to the National Green Tribunal
dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly
accepted.x: Section 5 empowers the Central Government to issue directions, including directions for closure of an industrial unit.
accepted.tq: Separate an environmental executive direction from powers belonging to constitutional or judicial authorities.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The National Ganga River Basin Authority, constituted in 2009, is an example of an authority constituted under:
o: Section 5 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
Section 16 of the Water Cess Act, 1977
accepted.x: The National Ganga River Basin Authority was an authority constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act.
accepted.tq: Use the section-number and body-name pairing to avoid confusing statutory authorities with constitutional bodies.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The Environment Protection Fund established under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act is maintained in the:
o: Public Account of the State concerned only
accepted.x: The Environment Protection Fund under Section 16 is maintained in the Public Account.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the three constitutional public-fund categories.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Environment Protection Fund:
1. It holds fines collected under the Air, Water and Environment Protection Acts.
2. Seventy-five per cent of the fund is allocated to States and Union Territories.
3. Twenty-five per cent is allocated to the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Fund receives fines under the three specified environmental laws, with 75% allocated to States and Union Territories and 25% to the Centre.
accepted.tq: Verify both the source of receipts and the percentage split before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 were notified by the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 were notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘which ministry handles this subject?’ test to reject neighbouring ministries.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Doon Valley notification was issued in 1989, not 1991. Revdanda Creek was also covered in 1989, while Dhanu Taluka was covered in 1991.
accepted.tq: Find the single shifted year in a list of closely related notifications.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The Doon Valley notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 prohibited industries that:
o: were located within 24 kilometres of the coast
used more than 24 metric tonnes of coal or fuel per day
accepted.x: The Doon Valley notification of 1989 prohibited industries burning more than 24 metric tonnes of coal or fuel a day.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the threshold figure and its subject from nearby location-based restrictions.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Revdanda Creek notification?
o: It permitted industries only after coastal ash dumping.
It prohibited industries around the creek.
It authorised power plants in ecologically fragile areas.
It introduced voluntary tree planting credits.
accepted.x: The Revdanda Creek notification of 1989 prohibited industries around the creek.
accepted.tq: Match the place-specific notification with its precise restriction.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The Coastal Regulation Zone notification issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 primarily:
o: regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping
requires prior clearance for all forest diversion
accepted.x: The CRZ notification of 1991 regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash and waste dumping in the regulated areas.
accepted.tq: Connect the environmental zone with its geographical subject and specific restriction.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the Dhanu Taluka notification?
o: It imposed a cess on water consumed by industries.
It declared the area ecologically fragile and prohibited power plants.
It established Central Pollution Control Boards.
It permitted unrestricted industrial development in coastal stretches.
accepted.x: The Dhanu Taluka notification of 1991 identified the area as ecologically fragile and prohibited power plants there.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific restriction to distinguish the notification from other environmental instruments.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The Environmental Impact Assessment notification under the Environment (Protection) Act is associated with:
accepted.x: The EIA notification was issued in 1994 and was subsequently revised in 2006; it provides for prior environmental clearance.
accepted.tq: Pair the original notification year with its later revision and the clearance requirement.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Prior environmental clearance is principally associated with which notification under the Environment (Protection) Act?
accepted.x: The EIA notification, first issued in 1994 and revised in 2006, provides for prior environmental clearance.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative requirement with the notification specifically designed for it.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s:
Which of the following instruments has been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications
2. Plastic Waste Management Rules
3. Green Credit Rules
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications, the Plastic Waste Management Rules and the Green Credit Rules are all instruments notified under the Environment (Protection) Act.
accepted.tq: Test whether the listed instruments belong to the umbrella Act rather than to a specialised statute.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Under the Green Credit Rules, 2023, voluntary tree planting on degraded land can earn:
accepted.x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 provide Green Credits for voluntary tree planting on degraded land.
accepted.tq: Match the environmental action with the exact official incentive term.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding standards under the Environment (Protection) Act is correct?
o: The Central Pollution Control Board publishes standards without any Central Ministry involvement.
Standards are notified only by the National Green Tribunal.
Standards are issued exclusively by local municipal bodies.
Standards are published in the Gazette by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with the Central Pollution Control Board.
accepted.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, in association with the Central Pollution Control Board, publishes standards in the Gazette.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership instead of assigning the function to a neighbouring authority.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The lead content in paints was capped at which level as an example of a standard under the Environment (Protection) Act?
accepted.x: Lead in paints was capped at 90 parts per million as an example of a standard published under the Act.
accepted.tq: Handle a numerical scale trap by checking the order of magnitude of the stated limit.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: What was the original maximum punishment provided under the Environment (Protection) Act for an offence?
o: Only a written warning issued by the Central Government
Up to 5 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence
Life imprisonment and forfeiture of all property
Up to 2 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000, with no continuing penalty
accepted.x: The original penalty was imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, with an additional Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence.
accepted.tq: Read the full penalty structure, including the continuing-offence component, rather than only the headline punishment.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

accepted.s: The penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act was decriminalised through the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
accepted.x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original criminal penalty provisions from their later legislative modification.
accepted.sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications
